pr_body:
##### Summary

This PR adds a collector that monitors all the AMD GPU cards on the system.

Fixes https://github.com/netdata/netdata/issues/12616.

The collector provides the following metrics:
- Utilization
  - [x] GPU utilization
  - [x] GPU memory utilization
- Clock frequencies:
  - [x] GPU clock frequency
  - [x] GPU memory clock frequency
- Memory usage:
  - [x] VRAM memory usage percentage
  - [x] VRAM memory usage
  - [x] visible VRAM memory usage percentage
  - [x] visible VRAM memory usage
  - [x] GTT memory usage percentage
  - [x] GTT memory usage


The following can be provided by `Sensors`, so they were not implemented:
- Power consumption
- Temperature
- Fan speed
- Voltage

Out of scope of this PR, but could potentially be implemented in the future (needs further research):
- PCIe RX/TX bandwidth metrics 
- Overclocking metrics
- Usage and consumption per process (similar to `nvtop`)
- Power state metrics

##### Test Plan

- Run this PR on a system without an AMD GPU and check that this branch behaves as `master`. 
- Run this PR on a system with an AMD GPU and check that all the above metrics are displayed. Check also that the "marketing name" for each GPU is correct (can be checked at the `product_name` label).

**For users: How does this change affect me?**

You will be able to monitor basic metrics for AMD GPUs. It does not affect any instances that do not have an AMD GPU (see the [nvidia-smi](https://www.netdata.cloud/nvidia-monitoring) collector for NVIDIA GPUs).

So a suggestion would be that if in case something is missing, don't give up on the whole card?

Also, if possible to capitalize the `amdgpu` entry in the list on the dashboard (e.g. `AMDGpu`) and an icon would be cool as well :-)

issue_context.body:
### Problem

There is currently no support for monitoring AMD GPUs.

### Description

Monitoring the utilization, frequencies and VRAM usage of AMD GPUs.

### Importance

really want

### Value proposition

Users can monitor their AMD GPU using Netdata.

### Proposed implementation

The relevant metrics are availabe in the sysfs, under /sys/class/drm/card*/device.

The kernel documentation has all the details:
https://docs.kernel.org/gpu/amdgpu/driver-misc.html
https://docs.kernel.org/gpu/amdgpu/thermal.html#gpu-sysfs-power-state-interfaces

Examples are available in the Arch Wiki: https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/AMDGPU?useskinversion=1#CLI_(default)

Additionally i have created a proof of concept that i currently use: https://gist.github.com/dokutan/b613187b5f80e53704f7901b23817ca9#file-amdgpu-chart-sh
Because my GPU doesn't support gpu_busy_percent (it fails with /sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_busy_percent: Operation not supported), i have omitted it.
